findings.title: Broken-Looking Radar
findings.problem: Radar is a solid dark disc with no visible rotating sweep line, no enemy/contact blips, only a static center triangle, appearing non-functional instead of operational.
findings.why: Players depend on radar for situational awareness in combat; a visually inactive radar creates uncertainty about whether the tool works, reducing trust in UI and gameplay clarity.
findings.fix: Add a thin, rotating cyan sweep line around the radar disc, plus small distinct dot markers for potential contacts (placeholders) to confirm the radar is active.

findings.title: Unmarked Road Progress Bar
findings.where: Road screen, top-center horizontal progress bar
findings.problem: The progress bar has only a single white indicator dot, no segmented markers or percentage labels, so remaining distance is unreadable at a glance.
findings.why: Highway travel requires immediate journey-length context; unclear progress leads to confusion about destination proximity, hurting pacing and player confidence.
findings.fix: Divide the bar into 10 equal segments (each =10% of total distance), color filled segments light gray, and keep the white dot to mark the current progress endpoint.

findings.title: Missing Armor Health Values
findings.where: Arena screen, right-side CONDITION panel (Armour section)
findings.problem: Each armor facing (front, rear, left, right, underbody) has only an empty dashed box, no numeric value or visual health indicator to show current integrity.
findings.why: Armor is critical survival currency in combat; without per-facing health data, players can’t quickly assess vehicle damage, leading to poor combat decisions.
findings.fix: Add a small numeric value (e.g., 15) and a color-coded micro-bar (green=intact, yellow=damaged, red=critical) next to each armor facing label for real-time context.

findings.title: Washed-Out Title Tagline
findings.problem: The white tagline text overlaps with the bright yellow sun glow, making parts of it faded and less readable.
findings.why: The tagline is the game’s core hook for new players; reduced contrast makes the title feel unpolished and hard to parse immediately.
findings.fix: Add a 1px dark brown drop shadow to the tagline text to boost contrast, and shift it slightly away from the sun’s center to avoid overlapping bright areas.

findings.title: Cramped Arena Top UI
findings.problem: Two key messages (controls: "WASD/arrows drive...", arena status: "Practice arena entered...") are stacked with no spacing, creating dense, hard-to-read text.
findings.why: Players need to reference controls and arena status at gameplay start; cramped text increases eye strain and slows quick comprehension of critical info.
findings.fix: Add vertical padding between the two top text boxes, or move the arena status to the top-left to keep controls as the primary top element with clear spacing.
